clauses.text: Section A — participating providers: annual deductible $1,000.00; annual out-of-pocket limit $5,000.00. No excess balance billing.
Section B — nonparticipating providers: annual deductible $2,000.00; annual out-of-pocket limit $10,000.00. Excess balance billing is permitted.

Calculation and accumulation rules: For covered care apply any remaining deductible first, then the stated copay, then member coinsurance to the remaining allowed amount. Round coinsurance half up to cents. Apply the remaining annual OOP cap to deductible, copay and coinsurance in that order. Only actually assessed covered sharing accrues. In- and out-of-network annual pools are separate. Permitted excess equals charge minus allowance and is outside OOP. Excluded care is full-charge patient liability outside deductible and OOP, with no insurer payment. No excess billing is allowed in network. A waived deductible means no deductible applies to that benefit.
B1: Low complexity visit (CPT/HCPCS 99212), in-network: covered; deductible waived; member copay $20.00; member coinsurance 0%.
B2: High complexity visit (CPT/HCPCS 99215), in-network: covered; deductible waived; member copay $70.00; member coinsurance 0%.

Rounding convention: Coinsurance is rounded half up to cents as an engine convention; the policy does not explicitly state rounding for coinsurance.
The policy includes a special provision for code-entry errors (line 16) that is not compiled as a benefit rule because it is a conditional liability adjustment, not a standard benefit.
coverage_gaps: Out-of-network benefits are not listed; only network-level deductible and OOP are provided.
No benefits for services other than the two listed office visits (e.g., urgent care, ER, drugs, imaging) are included.
The policy does not specify balance billing for out-of-network providers beyond the statement that excess balance billing is permitted; no specific billing protection language is provided.
The special provision for code-entry errors (line 16) is not compiled as a benefit rule because it is a conditional liability adjustment, not a standard benefit.
